transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM); Oliver (Procurement), Priya (InfoSec), Liam (Legal), Tess (FinOps), Marco (Platform)

Summary (auto):
- Discussed onboarding path for Skyline Retail: DPA redlines, MSA exceptions, SLA thresholds, pricing model and pilot scope.
- Key customer constraints: data residency, KMS/HSM, audit logs retention, and predictable p99 latency for peak retail events.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlines and SLA worksheet; legal-to-legal follow-up; short Dedicated pilot.

Topics: DPA redlines, MSA commercial exceptions, SLA p99 targets, KMS / HSM integration, pilot sizing and pricing, billing cadence and egress costs.

Action items listed above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time — Samir here from Redwood, AE — Jordan our SE is with me, and Maya from CSM. how's everyone?
[00:20] Oliver Grant: Hi, thanks. we should keep this super practical — procurement wants the gating items up front — e.g., what needs legal signoff, what needs security ok.
[00:32] Jordan Lee: Great. i'll jump into the tech bits when you hit pilot scope but high-level — we can offer Hosted, Dedicated, or Private (VPC/on-prem) options. for enterprise we usually recommend Dedicated for predictable p99 latencies.
[00:45] Priya Nair: quick note — we require customer-managed KMS or HSM for keys, and a full audit trail for token usage. also, data residency: EU-only for certain datasets.
[01:10] Samir Patel: understood. on the KMS part we support external KMS integrations (KMS providers) and there's an on-prem package. i'll put the KMS connector doc in the shared folder. (link)
[01:28] Marco Ruiz: when you say "external KMS" is that per-tenant keying or global? how do you handle key rotation?
[01:40] Jordan Lee: per-tenant is supported — rotation is customer-driven, we surface rotation hooks; there is an HSM-backed key wrap flow. i'll share the whitepaper.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: from legal — primary concerns are: indemnity caps, data processing terms in the DPA, and SLA credits. procurement likes clear exit/egress provisions.
[02:25] Tess Alvarez: and pricing — we need to model worst-case egress and token volume around holiday peaks — that can blow cost estimates.
[02:40] Samir Patel: absolutely — we can provide a pilot estimate. question for Tess — what's your expected QPS during peak windows and total monthly tokens for the pilot?
[02:58] Tess Alvarez: for a pilot we can commit to ~2M tokens/day and peak qps ~120 during a 2hr flash sale test.
[03:15] Jordan Lee: that helps a lot — for that profile Dedicated with autoscale burst is a good fit; it keeps the p99 tight while optimizing cost.
[03:38] Oliver Grant: procurement wants to know the billing cadence — monthly invoicing ok? and any minimums or commit?
[03:52] Samir Patel: Hosted is pay-as-you-go monthly; Dedicated typically has a reserved capacity commit — for pilots we can do a short-term reserved window or a time-limited trial with estimated cost credits. i'll propose options in the sheet.
[04:12] Priya Nair: security question — do you keep KV cache or prefix cache server-side? We need to ensure sensitive prefixes are never logged or stored.
[04:28] Jordan Lee: we do automatic KV cache for performance, but customers can opt out or configure prefix masking; logs can be redacted and we have audit log configs. full details in the security pack.
[04:47] Liam O'Connor: on the DPA redline, are there any standard exceptions you ask for? e.g., liability carveouts?
[04:58] Samir Patel: yes, typically we see ask for narrower data deletion timelines and more granular sub processors. we have a standard DPA but we are open to negotiated edits — i'll send our template with recommended language.
[05:20] Jordan Lee: quick technical caveat — for p99 latency we measure from request ingress to token emission; warm vs cold cache differences can show up. for the flash sale we recommend pre-warming KV caches for common prefixes.
[05:45] Priya Nair: does Redwood provide SOC2/ISO certs and pen test reports?
[05:55] Maya Chen: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 packages, and pen test summaries — i'll attach them.
[06:10] Oliver Grant: procurement will need the SLA table: uptime, p99, credits — is that standardized? or negotiable?
[06:25] Samir Patel: we have standard SLA tiers and credits; for Dedicated customers we can contract tighter SLOs with financial credits. i'll include the SLA spreadsheet and a plain-English mapping of SLO to credits.
[06:45] Tess Alvarez: want to confirm any egress or transfer fees — we operate in multi-cloud and egress costs can be additive.
[06:56] Jordan Lee: egress is billed separately in some configs; we'll call out egress and regional transfer fees in the pricing worksheet.
[07:12] Liam O'Connor: i did glance at your MSA and there's a payment net 45 clause—our finance prefers net 30. is that flexible?
[07:25] Samir Patel: we can put that into redlines — often payment terms are negotiable and can be aligned with procurement. we'll flag as a commercial exception.
[07:40] Marco Ruiz: operational question — during the pilot, who is on-call from Redwood if we see errors or performance regressions?
[07:52] Maya Chen: CSM + SE cover pilot support; Dedicated customers also get priority incident channel and optional SRE rotation for larger pilots.
[08:10] Oliver Grant: timeline — procurement wants vendor signoff within 3 weeks ideally. what are realistic dates for legal review and pilot start?
[08:28] Samir Patel: if we get DPA redlines and MSA exceptions this week, legal-to-legal can be next week, and pilot could start mid-February. so three weeks is tight but doable.
[08:45] Priya Nair: we need to validate data flows end-to-end — will there be a data processing diagram?
[08:56] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll provide a DPIA-style diagram and a sample audit log export.
[09:15] Tess Alvarez: about the pilot's data residency — some data will be EU-only, some global; can you pin nodes to eu-west-1 for sensitive traffic?
[09:30] Jordan Lee: yes, routing policies allow region pinning per-route; we can route EU-sensitive requests to eu region and non-sensitive to us-east.
[09:48] Oliver Grant: on encryption in transit and at rest — what cipher suites and rotation cadence?
[09:58] Jordan Lee: we use TLS1.2+/1.3, AES-256 at rest, and customer KMS handles rotation.
[10:15] Liam O'Connor: about auditability — we want retention for 3 years for certain logs. do you support extended retention?
[10:27] Maya Chen: yes, longer retention is available as an add-on; we'll include pricing.
[10:45] Samir Patel: switching to the DPA specifics — typical redlines we see: narrower processing purposes, subprocessor list updates, and breach notification SLAs. any redlines from Skyline up front?
[10:59] Liam O'Connor: we'll want the usual: 30 day breach notification, more specific processing purposes, and an option to audit subprocessors.
[11:12] Samir Patel: good — i'll draft those suggestions in our DPA and flag open items.
[11:30] Priya Nair: also, SSO integration — does Redwood support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[11:42] Jordan Lee: yes SAML + SCIM are supported; we'll provide docs and a small runbook for SSO setup.
[11:58] Tess Alvarez: pricing model question again — committed usage discounts vs variable usage — how does that work for Dedicated reserved capacity?
[12:12] Samir Patel: Dedicated has tiered commit discounts — higher commit -> larger discount; pilot-specific short commits can be shaped as time-limited reserved credits.
[12:30] Oliver Grant: can you provide example math for our peak test so procurement can approve?
[12:42] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll put a line-item estimate in the spreadsheet with assumptions: p99 target, qps, token counts, egress.
[13:00] Marco Ruiz: technical deep dive — are model variants supported for fallback if capacity is constrained? we want graceful degradation.
[13:12] Jordan Lee: yes, smart routing can fall back to lower-cost compatible model variants automatically; rollouts support canary/A-B.
[13:28] Oliver Grant: great. any competitor caveats we should note? we heard Anthropic quoted lower cost but less predictable p99s in public benchmarks.
[13:42] Samir Patel: competitors differ — we'll include a short comparison note but won't go deep.
[14:00] Liam O'Connor: procurement will want an exit plan — data export format, time to return/delete data, and final invoice timing.
[14:15] Samir Patel: standard is a 30-day export window; we can negotiate extended windows. we'll put explicit exit steps in the MSA.
[14:30] Tess Alvarez: one more on billing — do you support invoice line items per environment/team? we sometimes need project-level breakdown.
[14:42] Maya Chen: billing can include per-route/ per-team breakdowns; the Console has token-level cost allocation.
[15:00] Oliver Grant: okay let's talk pilot scope concretely — what are the minimum deliverables?
[15:10] Jordan Lee: deliverables: 1) Dedicated test cluster for 2 weeks, 2) instrumented tracing and logs shared to Skyline, 3) SLA baseline measurement, 4) security checklist completion.
[15:28] Priya Nair: and a threat model review + signoff before production.
[15:38] Samir Patel: agreed — we'll include threat model artifacts.
[16:00] Liam O'Connor: about indemnity caps — we prefer higher cap for regulated data; is that a deal-breaker?
[16:14] Samir Patel: we'll surface options; higher caps typically mean different commercial terms — i'll flag with sales leadership in the redline.
[16:28] Marco Ruiz: any constraints on model quantization or custom model uploads? we may want fine-tuned variants internally.
[16:40] Jordan Lee: Private/On-prem supports custom models; hosted supports curated open models and can host private variants under Dedicated with controls. there's an onboarding path for model ingestion.
[16:58] Tess Alvarez: ok we need the pricing sheet and pilot estimate asap — procurement wants to circulate tomorrow.
[17:12] Samir Patel: we'll prioritize. Jordan, Maya — can you get the SLA and pricing worksheet in the drive by end of day tomorrow?
[17:25] Jordan Lee: yes, i'll and i'll include sample perf logs and the p99 math.
[17:35] Maya Chen: i'll attach SOC2/ISO summaries and SSO runbook.
[17:50] Oliver Grant: final ask — can we get a one-page "what we need from Skyline" checklist so procurement can sign off quickly?
[18:02] Samir Patel: yes, we'll add a procurement-ready checklist: desired pilot dates, expected volumes, legal redlines, SSO contacts.
[18:18] Liam O'Connor: ok, perfect. let's reconvene after you send the docs.
[18:30] Samir Patel: recap: Samir to send redlines + commercial exceptions; Jordan to provide SLA/pricing + perf examples; Maya to provide security artifacts; schedule legal sync for next week.
[18:45] Oliver Grant: thanks everyone.
[18:52] Priya Nair: thanks.
[18:55] Meeting end.
